  "text": "The coats smelled of rain, though it had been dry for weeks. He pushed between them with his shoulder.

There was no keyhole in the plaster. There was a narrow crack, the sort his father filled each spring and blamed on the cold.

He put the key into it.

From the other side came the scrape of a chair.

“Before you turn it,” the man said, “ask her what happened to the first one.”

The boy looked back. Anne had drawn her hand into the cupboard. Only her eye remained.

“The first what?”

“The first boy who remembered.”

The woman bent to gather the broken stone. She cupped the pieces carefully, keeping the yellow lining upward.

“Don't answer him,” she said.

But Anne did.

“He grew up.”

The key moved a little beneath the boy's fingers. He had not turned it. Someone on the other side was trying to turn it for him.

He held it still.

“What was his name?”

Anne closed her eye.

Down the hall, the front door opened. His father called that he was home, then complained about the cold. He heard the familiar business of pockets being emptied: coins, matches, the heavy little knife used for cutting twine.

The man and woman stood very straight.

His father appeared in the doorway. He looked first at the stone, then at the boy's hand.

“I filled that,” he said.

The boy noticed the white dust caught beneath his father's nails.

Behind the plaster, the chair scraped again.

This time his father heard it too."
